newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: UKIO TO RAISE CAPITAL, ELECTS SWEDFUND MEMBER.
newsitem.headline: UKIO TO RAISE CAPITAL, ELECTS SWEDFUND MEMBER.

text.p: Lithuania's Ukio Bankas plans to boost its capital by a further 18 million litas with an issue of shares or a mix of shares and subordinated debt in the second half of the year, the bank said on Monday.
The bank said in a statement after a Saturday shareholder meeting that shareholders approved the planned capital rise.

"The bank has identified a need for further capital increase of 18 million litas in 1997 to expand lending acitivity, attract more funding, invest in the development of a debit card network and venture into leasing and the insurance business," Ukio said.
The bank also said it has elected the managing director of Swedfund to the bank, Olle Arefalk. Two other new board members were also elected: Byoung Hom Kim and In Hwan Song.
The bank said that it last increased its capital in December 1996 by 18 million litas and more than 50 percent of the bank is now owned by foreign investors.
